correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and hypotheses are explicit: m integer at least 2, all symmetric nonnegative stochastic 2m-by-2m kernels with allowed loops and only the prescribed edges. Averaging proves reduction over ALL feasible kernels to two weights. Orthogonal decomposition yields eigenvalues 1, 1-my, 1-(m-1)x-y (multiplicity 2m-4), and the explicit 2-by-2 odd block. For 2<=m<=7, its first column proves the global 1/sqrt(m) lower bound, achieved by a feasible rational choice; the remaining eigenvalue is bounded. For m>=8, the stated candidate has three active convex eigenvalue bounds and positive coefficients alpha,beta,gamma summing to one whose weighted gradients vanish, yielding a supporting-hyperplane global certificate; positivity follows from sqrt(m^2-8m+8)>2 and <m. Strictly positive multipliers force uniqueness of the invariant optimizer. The exact penalty follows by rationalization. The package checker independently constructs full matrices and verifies symbolically the nonstandard identities for tested integer values; no finite test is used to infer the all-m claim.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2004 and 2007 primary papers give the general SDP and symmetry framework and solve intact complete bipartite graphs; the 2006 path theorem covers the degenerate m=2 instance. Their results do not state the deleted-single-edge all-m formulas, the sharp transition at m=8, or the asymptotic deletion penalty. Their generic algorithms can compute individual finite instances, but do not imply these exact closed formulas without new two-orbit eigenvalue and positivity-certificate calculations. The searched external mathematical research records address many other deleted-edge or fastest-mixing graph families but no matching theorem. Residual specialized-literature risk remains.
residual_risks: Equivalent treatment of almost-complete bipartite fastest-mixing in unindexed specialized literature cannot be ruled out.
Full text of the Fill–Kahn comparison paper not inspected; the abstract points to paths, so its possible indirect implications remain unverified.
The 2007 general symmetry-SDP machinery is prior work and not claimed new; novelty is only its explicit single-edge-deletion solution and threshold.

value.rationale: This determines a natural all-m spectral optimization invariant of a minimally damaged dense network, with exact transition probabilities under an unrestricted global optimization, a sharp non-obvious dimension switch at m=8, and a quadratic-in-size loss 4/(9m^2) relative to the intact biclique. The result quantifies resilience of optimally designed reversible Markov mixing to one failed link and gives a usable closed-form redesign. It is not merely a numerical SDP solve, a parametrically renamed known graph, or a small isolated example; m>=3 is an infinite structural family.
